title: Prime-to-p torsors on a strict-local boundary puncture split at a finite root level
statement:
Let $p$ be prime and let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian regular local ring of characteristic $p$ [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Assume $R$ is strictly henselian, meaning henselian with separably closed residue field [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]. Let $t_1,\ldots,t_r$, $r\geq0$, be distinct members of a regular system of parameters of $R$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters]. Put $f=t_1\cdots t_r$ (empty product $1$) and $U=\operatorname{Spec}R[1/f]$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-ring-localization-away]. Let $G$ be a finite group with $p\nmid |G|$, and let $P\to U$ be a finite etale surjection [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-etale-morphism, def-weil-surjective-morphism] with an action of the constant group $G$ over $U$ which is simply transitive on every geometric fibre; equivalently it is a $G$-torsor [def-sbc-normal-dominant-galois]. No connectedness of $P$ is assumed.

There is an integer $n\geq1$ with $(n,p)=1$ such that, on putting
$$R_n=R[x_1,\ldots,x_r]/(x_1^n-t_1,\ldots,x_r^n-t_r),\qquad U_n=\operatorname{Spec}R_n[1/f],$$
using multivariate polynomial rings [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], the base change $P\times_U U_n$ is isomorphic over $U_n$ to the trivial torsor $\coprod_{g\in G}U_n$, with its regular $G$-action. The map $U_n\to U$ is induced by the displayed $R$-algebra structure. In particular, $r=0$ asserts that every such torsor over $\operatorname{Spec}R$ is trivial, with $n=1$.

source.place: Expose IX Proposition 2.1(i) and its strict-local parameter-root normal form, printed pp.133-134. Agent-formulated prime-to-p-group consequence: such torsors are tame, and the normal form is dominated by one finite simultaneous root cover. This is not a statement that a cover of prime-to-p degree without a prime-to-p Galois group is tame.

proof.text: Choose n = 1 if r = 0, and n = |G| otherwise. A finite group is nonempty, so n > 0. The prime-to-p group order and characteristic-p hypothesis make n coprime to p and a unit in R. Permute a regular system of parameters so that the given injective list comes first, followed by a tail.

source.place: IX Proposition 2.1(i), printed pp.133-134; assembly of the extracted subarguments.

proof.text: Put $B=R_n$. Apply [lem-sfb-henselian-parameter-root-regularity]: $R\hookrightarrow B$ is finite free and integral; $B$ is a strictly henselian regular local domain with residue field $R/\mathfrak m$ and parameters $x_1,\ldots,x_r,t_{r+1},\ldots,t_d$. Put $K=\operatorname{Frac}(R)$ and $E=\operatorname{Frac}(B)$.

source.place: IX Proposition 2.1(i), printed pp.133-134; assembly of the extracted subarguments.

proof.text: [lem-sfb-parameter-root-boundary-dvrs] gives all height-one boundary primes $(x_i)$ and finite injective DVR maps $R_{(t_i)}\to B_{(x_i)}=B\otimes_R R_{(t_i)}$ of root index $n$. Regular-local localization and regular normality make $R,B$ normal.

source.place: IX Proposition 2.1(i), printed pp.133-134; assembly of the extracted subarguments.

proof.text: Let $U_B=\operatorname{Spec}B[1/f]$ and $P_B=P\times_U U_B$. Apply [lem-sfb-pulled-torsor-normalization-model]. Its generic fields satisfy $[L_j:K]\mid n$, and $D=\prod_j(L_j\otimes_K E)=\prod_a F_a\ne0$. The finite algebra $C=\prod_a\overline B^{F_a}$ satisfies $C[1/f]=\Gamma(P_B,\mathcal O)$ with the actual structural maps.

source.place: IX Proposition 2.1(i), printed pp.133-134; assembly of the extracted subarguments.

proof.text: At every boundary prime $(x_i)$ apply [lem-sfb-kummer-normalization-boundary-etale] to those fields and the DVR map of step 3. It gives vanishing localized differentials, flatness over $B_{(x_i)}$, and etale source neighbourhoods of every point of $\operatorname{Spec}C$ above $(x_i)$.

source.place: IX Proposition 2.1(i), printed pp.133-134; assembly of the extracted subarguments.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-codimension-one-neighbourhood-etale-extension]. It constructs an open $W$ containing $U_B$ and all height-one points, and a finite etale $H\to\operatorname{Spec}B$ agreeing with $\operatorname{Spec}C$ on $W$. Hence $H_{U_B}\cong P_B$.

source.place: IX Proposition 2.1(i), printed pp.133-134; assembly of the extracted subarguments.

proof.text: The closed image of $H\to\operatorname{Spec}B$ contains the generic point, since $D\ne0$, so it is surjective. Apply [lem-sbc-finite-strict-henselian-algebra-etale-section] with base algebra $B$ over itself. Restrict the resulting section and use $H_{U_B}\cong P_B$ to obtain $s:U_B\to P_B$.

source.place: IX Proposition 2.1(i), printed pp.133-134; assembly of the extracted subarguments.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-finite-etale-torsor-section-trivialization] to the section of the actual pulled torsor. Compose its equivariant coproduct isomorphism with the normalization model comparison to the displayed pullback, using the comparison equations on both projections. For an empty boundary n was already chosen to be 1; the height-one boundary argument is vacuous. For a nonempty boundary the generic component degrees divide |G| = n.

source.place: IX Proposition 2.1(i), printed pp.133-134; assembly of the extracted subarguments.

proof_origin.place: IX Proposition 2.1(i), printed pp.133-134; Lean assembly from the six existing extracted subarguments. The exponent is chosen as 1 at the start for an empty boundary; generic-component divisibility is used only at actual boundary primes.

tool_uses.why: Regular-local localization is needed only to certify normality for the generic-normalization input; no six-functor assertion is substituted.
Regular rings are normal; this is the coefficient-free algebraic prerequisite of the normalization model.
The finite etale extension has closed image, so its nonempty generic fibre proves surjectivity.
Once the root ring is strictly henselian, this tool supplies a section of the surjective etale extension; it does not supply the root cover or its equivariant trivialization.
